headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: agentic-flow can use MCP/stdin-stdout while RD-Agent sends data to third-party APIs and logs outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agentic-flow exposes stdin/stdout and MCP, so if RD-Agent outputs are bridged into it, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. RD-Agent also uses browsers and broad network egress, increasing the chance that untrusted content enters the pairwise flow. The shared channel is not documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF RD-Agent outputs are copied into agentic-flow via stdin/stdout or MCP, injection becomes plausible.
IF the orchestrator forwards browser-sourced text from RD-Agent into agentic-flow without sanitization, instructions may be hijacked.
mitigations: Disable direct text handoff between agents.
Add a strict allowlist for fields passed through MCP.
Strip imperative language from RD-Agent outputs before forwarding.
Use a human review step for any browser-derived content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every inter-agent message.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agentic-flow touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures, while RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and API keys. RD-Agent’s broad API use and agentic-flow’s MCP/stdin-stdout create a plausible path for sensitive data to leave the workspace or be exposed across the pair. The blast radius includes secrets and sensitive reports.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or log directory, sensitive files can be read across the pair.
IF RD-Agent forwards its context to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek APIs while ingesting agentic-flow outputs, leakage can occur.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and log directories.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
Block secrets from inter-agent messages.
Restrict RD-Agent API calls to non-sensitive inputs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agentic-flow can execute shell commands, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; RD-Agent runs browsers and uses multiple APIs. If both operate on the same repository or mutable workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can conflict. RD-Agent’s Docker isolation reduces but does not eliminate overlap because the shared target is not documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout, concurrent commits or file edits may race.
IF RD-Agent browser-driven tasks write artifacts into the same directory as agentic-flow, overwrites can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize git writes with a lock.
Disable parallel runs on the same repo.
Review and merge changes manually before commit.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level mutexes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agentic-flow can generate prompts, explanations, and metrics, and RD-Agent can consume outputs while also taking browser/API actions. If RD-Agent treats agentic-flow output as authoritative, an error or hallucination can cascade into downstream research actions or logged results. Because no verification step is documented between them, the safer choice is the higher severity.
conditions: IF RD-Agent ingests agentic-flow output without validation, errors can propagate into research artifacts.
IF agentic-flow emits malformed instructions that RD-Agent executes via browser/API tools, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before RD-Agent consumes agentic-flow output.
Require schema checks on all inter-agent messages.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only mode for untrusted inputs.
Log and diff every handoff between agents.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: agentic-flow handles task prompts and repository metadata, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and multiple third-party APIs. That combination creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention, residency, and third-party processing, especially because RD-Agent is documented to send data to external model providers. The pairwise compliance path is inferred from docs, not directly verified.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated reports are processed by RD-Agent APIs, residency or DPA obligations may be triggered.
IF agentic-flow stores prompts longer than RD-Agent logs, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Block regulated data from external API calls.
Set explicit retention limits for logs and prompts.
Confirm vendor DPAs for each API provider.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
